notes:
Follow-up: kinodynamics-full environment sensitivity (2026-11-04)
A controlled comparison of PR #469 head 45172046 and shared-linearization commit
f71c907d found no regression. With the successful investigation's NumPy 2.2.6
environment, both complete five iterations and every saved result array is exact.
The final objective is 9120.017395552624; equality L2 is 4.1370e-12 and inequality
L2 is 1.2862e-7. Optimization times are 81.61 s and 81.16 s on one pinned CPU.
These are individual reproduction runs, not a new statistical timing comparison.

Both revisions fail under the original benchmark's Python environment with
NumPy 2.5.2, reporting the same cone-QP AL failure already shown in the table.
A further run keeps the successful interpreter, binaries, inputs, and settings
and replaces only the imported NumPy package (including its numerical backend)
with NumPy 2.5.2: it reproduces the exact same failure. Initial Values then match
the failing environment byte-for-byte. Their maximum local-coordinate difference
from the successful initialization is 3.67e-9 (mixed variable units).

This establishes environment-dependent numerical sensitivity in the existing
solver, not a regression from f71c907d. It does not identify the precise NumPy
operation responsible, nor prove which inner AL stopping condition was reached.
The reported AL stationarity 1.18637e-6 exceeds the configured 1e-7 tolerance;
violation 3.4788e-12 is below the 1e-9 feasibility tolerance. The failure correctly
remains recorded; it is not a missing result or evidence of changed refactor
behavior. A robustness fix needs its own focused reproducer and fresh validation.
No solver code, tolerances, or old benchmark measurements were changed.
Full reproduction notes: gtdynamics/cmcopt/KinodynamicsFailureInvestigation.md.

Final result
All 318 cases have before/after outcomes. The 250 completed cases each have five
measured trials per version; all saved numerical comparisons are exact. The
remaining 68 cases reproduce baseline failures: 32 timeouts, four crashes and
32 explicit solver failures. No completed case changes solution quality.

Timings are essentially unchanged within the measured workloads. The three
initial >5% flags have recheck ratios of 0.9932, 1.0007 and 0.9995. The independent
basis-retractor recheck takes 209.44 s before and 209.33 s after. The longer
quadruped case is 73.85 s before and 74.77 s after; fixed-dynamics modes are within
0.3%, and the one-iteration full clip is within 0.8%. These results support the
ownership simplification without establishing a useful speedup.

Scope and baseline
The checkpoint f71c907d already uses component coordinates for the global linear
solve. This change simplifies ownership and indexing. It does not repeat the
earlier constrained-solver replacement or claim its previously reported 2.4x gain.
No compatibility aliases or alternative old paths remain for the removed APIs.
The separate coupled objective and component-local nonlinear retractions remain.

Native validation
Fourteen test targets pass: testWorkingFace, testIELMWorkingSet,
testIEManifoldLinearization, testIEConstraintManifold, testTangentCone,
testIEManifoldOptimizer, testCMCImprovements, testReducedALRetractor,
testArticulatedRetractor, testAffineProjection, testIEHalfSphere,
testReducedALRetractionValidation, testRobustQp, and testWorldVelocityFactor.
The working-set oracle checks 64 coupled problems against exhaustive constrained
QR. The direct component tests also check original indices, boundary tie order,
step bounds, row release, derivative sharing and state lifetime.
Four Python integration tests pass. Both full-dynamics binaries pass their
wrench, friction and boundary Jacobian self-tests.
testIERetractor and testIEQuadrupedUtilsManifold are disabled in the repository's
CMake configuration; they are not counted as passes. SuiteSparse is disabled.

Inventory and measurement
The inventory covers all 15 rss/yetong CMC programs, their active LM/GD/CM
comparisons, Yetong08 multistage and retractor variants, and Yetong09 fixed and
varying metrics plus the independently runnable second retractor: 25 native cases. The G1 grid adds 288 cases: 24 recorded states,
four friction formulations, three retractors. Five walking cases cover fixed
kinematics (hard and soft base balance), full coupled kinodynamics, a one-iteration
full-clip diagnostic and a five-iteration short clip. Total: 318 cases.
Other search hits are wrappers, exporters or plots of these same problems.
Commented-out experiments and CM-only main_connected_poses are identified in
the suite README; they are not additional active CMC experiments.

Release Clang 18.1.3 and the same GTSAM build are used for both snapshots.
Runs alternate baseline/candidate order, with one warmup and five measured
successful runs. Each pair is pinned to the same logical CPU on separate physical
cores (native primarily CPU 2; grid CPUs 4/6/8/10; walking CPUs 4/10).
Yetong09/10/11 use CPUs 12/14/16 respectively. The independent basis-retractor
case warms up on CPU 12, then distributes its five repeated pairs across CPUs
0/4/6/8/10 concurrently. Each pair uses the same core before and after; its
timings describe that concurrent-pair workload, not an isolated production run.
OMP_NUM_THREADS and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS are 1. Affinity also limits TBB and avoids
oversubscription. Kinodynamics still configures eight retraction workers, sharing
that CPU. Production eight-core app latency requires a separate measurement.
Native scripts report optimization only. Fixed dynamics includes its native
construction and solve; coupled kinodynamics reports native optimization.
Timing scopes are compared only within a case. GP preparation and Python/model
loading are excluded from those primary comparisons.

The benchmark skips the legacy helper's optional post-solve re-optimization of
saved iterates for projected-cost diagnostics. This never enters the reported
optimization time or changes the optimized result. Some early Yetong07 trials
still ran those diagnostics, so their helper/process wall times are not comparable;
the optimization times and numerical comparisons are comparable.
Failure trials already in progress when the timeout policy was adopted can have
different trial counts in the two versions; both outcomes remain recorded.
Two initial >5% G1 timing flags were rerun in fresh alternating batches on CPU 12.
The independent basis-retractor batch also exceeded that threshold: its first
half overlapped the last generic-retractor timeout, and its second half ran
faster for both versions. A fresh five-pair batch repeats it under steady load,
using the already completed warmup. Both batches remain in the report. The JSON
also includes individual paired ratios, allowing run-order drift to be inspected.

Known baseline problems
RSS04 LM/CM and Yetong10/11 segfault in both versions. The RSS04 backtrace reaches
NonlinearFactorGraph::error during initial IELM state construction. Yetong10 also
fails at a null instruction address after printing a factor-graph size. These
failures occur before a completed solve; their root cause is not established here.
Matching failures do not establish solution equivalence for those examples.
Yetong08's multistage run times out at 600 seconds before completing its first
stage in both versions. A paired warmup timeout is recorded as censored without
repeating the same timeout five times. G1 full-dynamics has a 30-second watchdog;
its failed/censored configurations remain visible in the table and JSON.
Thirty grid configurations time out in both versions. Another 31 reduced-barrier
configurations return the same explicit solver error: "Reduced projection result
violates original constraints or blocking faces". The native line-oriented API
returns exit status zero with that JSON error; the report correctly counts the
error response as a failure, rather than a completed solution.
The full five-iteration G1 clip reproduces the pre-existing local cone-QP AL
fallback failure: stationarity 1.18637e-6, violation 3.4788e-12, 19 iterations.
The full one-iteration and short five-iteration cases supplement this failure;
they do not establish convergence of the complete five-iteration full clip.

Reproducibility and exclusions
The embedded provenance records the checkpoint, GTSAM revision, library hashes,
request fingerprint and source fingerprints. Raw numerical arrays and logs are
retained in /tmp/cmc-controlled-{before,after}, /tmp/cmc-final-g1-{before,after},
and /tmp/cmc-final-walk-{before,after}. The checked-in drivers reproduce the
inventory and comparison without requiring these temporary paths.
Early exploratory timing batches with TBB oversubscription, stale binary RPATH,
and incomplete Python snapshot packaging were discarded. They are not counted
as algorithm failures or included in the reported timings.
